description: Hi everyone!For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, I am forming a team.Our goal is to craft a compelling, historically accurate, and interactive experience that highlights the legacy of humanity's hardware left behind on lunar and Martian surfaces. We aim to combine space data, historical archives, and creative media to showcase where these artifacts rest. To bring this vision to life, I am looking for enthusiastic teammates with a mix of creative and technical skills.
summary: The project examines the mission of NASA's InSight Lander, which operated on Mars from 2018 to 2022 to study the planet's deep interior. Operating as a stationary explorer at Elysium Planitia, InSight utilized precision instruments—such as a seismometer, heat probe, and radio science antennas—to analyze the Martian crust, mantle, and core. Over the course of its mission, the lander detected 1,319 marsquakes, mapped a three-layer crust, and measured a fully molten iron core. Although accumulated dust eventually caused a loss of power and concluded the mission in December 2022, the seismic data collected continues to help scientists map safe landing sites for future human exploration.
details:
Here is a minimized summary of the project details:

  • What it does: The InSight lander acts as a planetary doctor, using instruments like a seismometer (SEIS) and heat probe to take Mars's vital signs and study its deep interior.
  • Benefits & Impact: It discovered over 1,319 marsquakes, mapped a 3-layer crust, and measured a fully molten iron core. Its data helps scientists understand how rocky planets form and aids in selecting safe landing sites for future human missions.
  • Technology & Hardware: It utilized a stationary deck, high-sensitivity scientific instruments, a robotic arm, and solar panels that operated from 2018 until dust accumulation ended the mission in December 2022.
